contributions.title: Efficient relative-position self-attention
contributions.description: The authors propose extending Transformer self-attention to incorporate relative positions or distances between sequence elements and describe the approach as efficient.

contributions.title: Relation-aware formulation
contributions.description: The authors cast relative-position attention as a special case of attention over arbitrary pairwise input relations, identifying labeled, directed graph modeling as future work.

contributions.title: Translation improvements and comparison of position representations
contributions.description: The authors report improvements over absolute position representations on two WMT 2014 translation tasks and report no additional benefit from combining relative and absolute representations.

contributions.title: Relation-aware self-attention
contributions.description: The authors propose extending self-attention to represent pairwise relationships between input elements as edges in a labeled, directed, fully connected graph.

contributions.title: Relative position representations
contributions.description: The authors claim relative position representations for self-attention and state that these representations are invariant to total sequence length.

contributions.title: Edge-aware self-attention
contributions.description: The authors extend self-attention to incorporate edge representations into both the sublayer output and attention compatibility computations, using addition to facilitate efficient implementation.

contributions.title: Learned representations of clipped relative positions
contributions.description: For linear sequences, the authors represent pairwise relative positions using learned edge representations and clip distances to a maximum absolute value k.

contributions.title: Efficient relative-position self-attention
contributions.description: The authors claim an efficient extension of Transformer self-attention that incorporates relative positions or distances. The supplied reading units describe sharing relative representations, splitting attention computation, and implementing the relative terms through tensor reshaping and parallel matrix multiplication.

contributions.title: Translation improvements from relative position representations
contributions.description: The authors claim improvements over absolute position representations on two WMT 2014 translation tasks and report that combining absolute and relative positions provides no further benefit.

contributions.title: Efficient relative-position self-attention
contributions.description: The authors claim an efficient extension of Transformer self-attention that incorporates relative positions or distances between sequence elements.

contributions.title: General relation-aware self-attention
contributions.description: The authors claim that the mechanism can represent arbitrary pairwise input relationships, with potential application to graph-labeled inputs.

contributions.title: Translation improvements from relative position representations
contributions.description: The authors claim translation improvements over absolute position representations on two WMT 2014 tasks and report no further benefit from combining absolute and relative position representations.

contributions.title: Empirical evaluation of relative position representations in machine translation
contributions.description: The authors report translation improvements over their baseline using relative position representations, no observed benefit from additionally including sinusoidal position encodings, and limited sensitivity to relative-distance clipping once k is at least 2.

contributions.title: Relative-position representations in Transformer self-attention
contributions.description: The authors claim an extension of Transformer self-attention that incorporates relative positions or distances between sequence elements. The supplied reading units examine its sensitivity to clipping distance and the contributions of its two relative-position representations.

contributions.title: Relative-position extension to self-attention
contributions.description: The authors present an extension to self-attention that incorporates relative position information for sequences and claim that it improves machine translation performance.

claims.statement: The proposed extension incorporates representations of relative positions or distances between sequence elements into Transformer self-attention.
The proposed relative-position self-attention has an efficient implementation.
The relative-position mechanism can be formulated as a special case of self-attention incorporating arbitrary relations between pairs of input elements.
On WMT 2014 English-to-German translation, the approach improves performance by 1.3 BLEU over absolute position representations.
On WMT 2014 English-to-French translation, the approach improves performance by 0.3 BLEU over absolute position representations.
Relative position representations improve translation quality on both reported tasks even when they entirely replace absolute position encodings.
Combining relative and absolute position representations yields no further improvement in translation quality.
The proposed extension represents pairwise input relationships using a labeled, directed, fully connected graph.
Each edge has two learned representations, aV_ij and aK_ij, intended for use in the output and compatibility computations, respectively, without additional linear transformations.
The edge representations can be shared across attention heads, and the authors set their dimensionality da equal to the attention-head output dimensionality dz.
The authors' relative position representations are invariant to total sequence length.
The modified sublayer output propagates edge information by adding a value-side edge representation to each projected input value before attention-weighted aggregation.
Attention compatibility incorporates edge information by adding a key-side edge representation to the projected key in the scaled query–key computation.
Simple addition of edge representations in the output and compatibility equations enables an efficient implementation.
Clipping relative position differences to the interval from −k to k produces 2k + 1 distinct edge labels.
Separate learned key-side and value-side relative-position representations are indexed by the clipped displacement j − i.
Clipping relative distances enables the model to generalize to sequence lengths not encountered during training.
The authors hypothesize that precise relative-position information is not useful beyond a certain distance.

Sharing relative position representations across attention heads reduces their storage complexity from O(h n² d_a) to O(n² d_a); sharing them across sequences gives the stated overall self-attention space complexity O(b h n d_z + n² d_a), compared with O(b h n d_z) without relative representations.
The attention compatibility calculation can be split into an ordinary query–key term and a relative-position term, allowing computation without broadcasting relative position representations.

Tensor reshaping permits the relative-position compatibility term to be computed using n parallel multiplications of b h × d_z and d_z × n matrices; further reshaping permits addition to the ordinary attention term, and the same approach applies to the output computation.

In the reported machine translation experiments, the implementation decreases steps per second by 7% while maintaining the same model and batch sizes on P100 GPUs as the Vaswani et al. reference configuration.

For the base Transformer on newstest2014, the supplied result extraction reports that replacing absolute with relative position representations increases English-to-German BLEU from 26.5 to 26.8 and English-to-French BLEU from 38.2 to 38.7.

For the big Transformer on newstest2014, the supplied result extraction reports that replacing absolute with relative position representations increases English-to-German BLEU from 27.9 to 29.2 and English-to-French BLEU from 41.2 to 41.5.
Adding absolute position representations to relative position representations provides no further translation benefit.
The relative-position method is instantiated in the base model with clipping distance k = 16 and unique edge representations for each layer and attention head.
The relative-position method is instantiated in the big model with clipping distance k = 8 and unique edge representations for each layer.
The extension incorporates relative position information efficiently.
The relation-aware mechanism can represent arbitrary pairwise input relationships.
The mechanism is potentially applicable to graph-labeled inputs.

The translation experiment compares a model using only relative position representations with a Transformer baseline using sinusoidal position encodings, with baseline results generated to isolate the effect of relative positions.
Relative position representations improve translation performance over absolute position representations on two WMT 2014 tasks.
Adding absolute position representations to relative position representations provides no further translation benefit.
Relative position representations improve English-to-German translation over the authors' baseline by 0.3 BLEU in the base configuration.
Relative position representations improve English-to-German translation over the authors' baseline by 1.3 BLEU in the big configuration.
Relative position representations improve English-to-French translation over the authors' baseline by 0.5 BLEU in the base configuration.
Relative position representations improve English-to-French translation over the authors' baseline by 0.3 BLEU in the big configuration.
The authors observed no benefit from adding sinusoidal position encodings to relative position representations in their experiments.

In the base-model clipping experiment without absolute position representations, BLEU on the WMT English-to-German newstest2013 development set varies little across the tested clipping distances k ≥ 2.
The method contains two relative-position representations, aV_ij in equation (3) and aK_ij in equation (4), whose contributions the authors evaluate through ablation.

In the reported clipping-distance experiment, BLEU varies little for k ≥ 2: the extracted rows report 25.8, 25.9, 25.8, 25.9, and 25.8 for k = 2, 4, 16, 64, and 256, respectively, compared with 25.5 for k = 1.
Relative-position representations used solely to determine compatibility between elements may suffice for the reported evaluation; whether this holds for other tasks remains unresolved.
The proposed self-attention extension incorporates relative position information for sequences.
The proposed relative-position extension improves machine translation performance.
The extracted ablation results report 25.8 BLEU both when aV_ij and aK_ij are enabled and when only aK_ij is enabled.
The extracted ablation results report 25.3 BLEU when only aV_ij is enabled.
The extracted ablation results report 12.5 BLEU when both aV_ij and aK_ij are disabled.
